newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine police suspend "Dirty War" doctor.
newsitem.headline: Argentine police suspend "Dirty War" doctor.

text.p: An Argentine police doctor accused of torturing pregnant women in the "Dirty War" of the late 1970s, and of selling babies for adoption, was suspended from service on Friday, authorities said.

The Medical Commissioner of the Police of Buenos Aires Province, Jorge Berges, had become a symbol of impunity for his alleged crimes and was shot 20 times last April by gunmen suspected to belong to a small leftist guerrilla band.
They then planted a bomb outside the hospital where he was recovering after falling into a coma, but failed to kill him.
Berges earned the nickname "the Argentine Mengele" for torturing and experimenting on female detainees in the brutal campaign against suspected leftists during the military regime of 1976-83.

After the return of democracy, he was sentenced to 6-1/2 years in prison in 1986 but was released three years later under a general amnesty for "Dirty War" criminals granted by President Carlos Menem and eventually became police medical commissioner in Buenos Aires.
Berges was also under investigation for selling two babies of a couple kidnapped and presumably killed by the military in 1977, but never came to trial for those charges.

Berges' suspension without pay came as part of a broader clean-up of Argentina's biggest police force by provincial governor Eduardo Duhalde, after it was tainted by corruption, drugs, links with anti-Jewish bomb attacks and the recent murder of a news photographer.
